newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. so far approves eight food contracts for Iraq.
newsitem.headline: U.N. so far approves eight food contracts for Iraq.

text.p: The U.N. Iraqi sanctions committee has so far approved eight out of 20 contracts for humanitarian supplies submitted to it under an "oil-for-food" deal that went into effect last December, the United Nations said on Wednesday.

U.N. spokesman Fred Eckhard said the latest four contracts approved were for: infant formula from Tunisia worth $4.3 million; infant formula from France worth $1.6 million; $900,000 worth of medical supplies from Britain; and wheat from France worth $21 million.
A total of 187 sales applications had so far been received by the U.N. secretariat, the spokesman added.

Under the "oil-for-food" deal, Iraq may sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to buy food, medicine and other humanitarian supplies to help offset the effects of sanctions imposed after Iraq invased Kuwait in August 1990.
Eckhard also said 37 out of 151 international observers have so far arrived in Baghdad to monitor the distribution of the supplies.
Although they had to travel overland from Amman, Iraq had now given permission for remaining observers and other U.N. personnel to fly directly into Baghdad airport, he said.
